scope: Cross-paper duplicate / near-duplicate concern detection across all 817 reviewer_concerns.

method.primary: difflib.SequenceMatcher.ratio() over concern_text, exhaustive within each of 13 categories (cross-paper only).
method.secondary: token-Jaccard with stopword stripping, also clustered by category.
method.pair_count_evaluated: approximately 46k cross-paper pairs after category clustering (down from 333k all-pairs).
method.short_circuit: length-ratio < 0.5 skipped to keep runtime sane.
method.source_agent_attribution: concern_id -> extracting agent map built from paper/extraction-wave-2026-05-13/agent-*.json (covers the 394 wave concerns; 423 original-curated concerns have no source agent).

headline_finding: Zero cross-paper concern pairs reach SequenceMatcher >= 0.85, zero reach token-Jaccard >= 0.7, and zero verbatim duplicates exist across papers. The 2026-05-13 extraction wave shows no evidence of agent copy-paste contamination: even when restricted to within-same-extracting-agent pairs, zero pairs cross 0.7 similarity. Concern texts are highly heterogeneous because each reviewer quotes paper-specific specifics (cohort names, model names, exact metrics). Canonical patterns exist at the SEMANTIC level (same category + same gates across many papers) but not at the TEXTUAL level, which is the expected and desired shape for RAG.

highest_similarity_cross_paper_pairs_for.concern_text_a: Missing data shown not to be MCAR. Imputation method doesn't handle MNAR. Need reporting of N missing and bias analysis.
highest_similarity_cross_paper_pairs_for.concern_text_b: Missing data in EHR shown to be MNAR; imputation method does not address this; missingness counts and potential bias not fully reported.
highest_similarity_cross_paper_pairs_for.note: Below the 0.85 threshold; included for transparency.

highest_similarity_cross_paper_pairs_for.concern_text_a: Model trained on single-center data. Needs external validation across different transplant centers with different protocols.
highest_similarity_cross_paper_pairs_for.concern_text_b: Single-channel oximetry is simpler than polysomnography but external validation across different oximeters and populations needed.
highest_similarity_cross_paper_pairs_for.note: Below the 0.85 threshold; included for transparency.

recommendations: No KB edits required for cross-paper duplication. The corpus is clean of agent copy-paste.

The 49 canonical-pattern groups (>=3 distinct papers sharing category+gates signature) ARE the high-value RAG retrieval targets. Consider adding a derived field `canonical_pattern_id` per concern that points back to one of these groups, so RAG can answer "what is the typical reviewer concern about external_validation?" by retrieving the group rather than individual paraphrases.

Top 3 canonical RAG-relevant patterns (by paper count): (1) study_design + cohort_definition_gate (45 papers) — temporal/inclusion ambiguity; (2) evaluation_metrics + evaluation_quality_gate (27 papers) — CI/calibration/AUROC interpretation; (3) model_selection + model_selection_audit_gate (26 papers) — cross-validation vs random-split, hyperparameter selection.

Negative result confirms agent-level extraction quality: the 9 wave agents each produced lexically distinct outputs even on the same review categories, indicating they paraphrased from source PDFs rather than templating.
